after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: When a content author edits text content in the CMS, the corresponding text on the live preview page updates in real-time without a manual page refresh.
When a content author edits rich-text content in the CMS, the corresponding formatted text on the live preview page updates in real-time without a manual page refresh.
When a content author edits a link in the CMS, the rendered clickable link on the live preview page updates in real-time without a manual page refresh.
When a content author changes an image in the CMS, the rendered image on the live preview page updates in real-time without a manual page refresh.
When a content author edits a table in the CMS, the rendered table on the live preview page updates in real-time without a manual page refresh.

notes: Story requests a new Live Preview capability for CMS content. The central attachment point is useContent (src/hooks/useContent.ts), which is the single hook through which 236+ consumers retrieve Contentstack content via getContentByKey(). Integrating Live Preview there propagates updates to all downstream components without touching them individually. Contentstack external services are unreachable at test time, so VCs are written to the boundary with mocked assumptions.

notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a useful architectural note about useContent being the central integration point for 236+ consumers. I built the full AC list from scratch based on the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the three-site scope (GO, UP, MX), and the identified files. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 sets a 5-second SLA for preview updates based on typical WebSocket latency expectations — this may need adjustment based on actual Contentstack Live Preview SDK behavior. (2) AC-7 ensures preview infrastructure is completely absent in production builds — critical security requirement. (3) AC-8 addresses rapid-edit debouncing to prevent render storms. (4) AC-11 ensures cross-site isolation since all three sites share the same codebase but have separate Contentstack stacks. (5) AC-9 and AC-13 address resource cleanup. CAVEAT: I did not have access to the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, or ContentstackLink.tsx. If Live Preview is already partially implemented, or if the architecture differs from openspec's description (e.g., useContent does not exclusively use getContentByKey, or ContentstackLink has its own data fetching), some ACs may need adjustment. I recommend reviewing these ACs against the actual source before implementation.
